type="bold">27. </hi>Et septem vaccae vacuae et turpes, ascendentes post eas, septem anni sunt: et septem spicae vacuae arefactae Euro, erunt septem anni famis.<div eID="gen5097" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen5098" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">28. </hi>This <hi type="italic">is</hi> the thing which I have spoken unto Pharaoh: What God <hi type="italic">is</hi> about to do he sheweth unto Pharaoh.<div eID="gen5098" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen5099" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">28. </hi>Hoc est verbum quod liquutus sum ad Pharaonem, guod Deus facit, videre fecit Pharaonem.<div eID="gen5099" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen5100" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">29. </hi>Behold, there come seven years of great plenty throughout all the land of Egypt:<div eID="gen5100" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen5101" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">29. </hi>Ecce, septem anni veniunt abundantiae magnae in omni terra Aegypti.<div eID="gen5101" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen5102" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">30. </hi>And there shall arise after them seven years of famine; and all the plenty shall be forgotten in the land of Egypt; and the famine shall consume the land;<div eID="gen5102" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen5103" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">30. </hi>Et surgent septem anni famis post eos: et erit in oblivione omnis abundantia in terra Aegypti, et consumet fames terram.<div eID="gen5103" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen5104" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">31. </hi>And the plenty shall not be known in the land by reason of that famine following; for it <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> very grievous.<div eID="gen5104" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen5105" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">31. </hi>Nec cognoscetur abundantia in terra, propter famem ipsam se quentem, quia gravis erit valde.<div eID="gen5105" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen5106" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">32. </hi>And for that the dream was doubled unto Pharaoh twice; <hi type="italic">it is</hi> because the thing <hi type="italic">is</hi> established by God, and God will shortly bring it to pass.<div eID="gen5106" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen5107" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">32. </hi>Propterea vero iteratum est somnium ipsi Pharaoni duabus vicibus, quia firma est res a Deo, et festinat Deus facere eam.<div eID="gen5107" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen5108" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">33. </hi>Now therefore let Pharaoh look out a man discreet and wise, and set him over the land of Egypt.<div eID="gen5108" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen5109" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">33. </hi>Nune igitur provideat Pharaovirum prudentem, et sapientem, et constituant illum super terram Aegypti.<div eID="gen5109" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen5110" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">34. </hi>Let Pharaoh do <hi type="italic">this</hi>, and let him appoint officers over the land, and take up the fifth part of the land of Egypt in the seven plenteous years.<div eID="gen5110" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen5111" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">34. </hi>Faciat Pharao, et praeficiat praefectos super terram, et quintam partem sumat a terra Aegypti in septem annis abundantiae.<div eID="gen5111" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen5112" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">35. </hi>And let them gather all the food of those good years that come, and lay up corn under the hand of Pharaoh, and let them keep food in the cities.<div eID="gen5112" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen5113" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">35. </hi>Et congregent totam annonam horum annorum bonorum qui venient, congregent, inquam, frumentum sub manu Pharaonis, cibum in urbibus, et servent.<div eID="gen5113" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen5114" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">36. </hi>And that food shall be for store to the land against the seven years of famine, which shall be in the land of Egypt; that the land perish not through the famine.<div eID="gen5114" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen5115" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">36. </hi>Et erit cibus in depositum pro terra, pro septem annis famis qui erunt in terra Aegypti: ita non succidetur terra propter famem.<div eID="gen5115" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen5116" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">37. </hi>And the thing was good in the eyes of Pharaoh, and in the eyes of all his servants.<div eID="gen5116" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen5117" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">37. </hi>Placuit sermo in oculis Pharaonis, et in oculis omnium servorum ejus.<div eID="gen5117" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen5118" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">38. </hi>And Pharaoh said unto his servants, Can we find <hi type="italic">such a one</hi> as this <hi type="italic">is</hi>, a man in whom the Spirit of God <hi type="italic">is</hi>?<div eID="gen5118" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen5119" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">38. </hi>Et dixit Pharao ad servos suos, Num inveniemus talem virum, in quo Spiritus Dei?<div eID="gen5119" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen5120" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">39. </hi>And Pharaoh said unto Joseph, Forasmuch as God hath shewed thee all this, <hi type="italic">there is</hi> none so discreet and wise as thou <hi type="italic">art</hi>:<div eID="gen5120" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen5121" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">39. </hi>Dixit ergo Pharao ad Joseph, Postquam cognoscere fecit Deus to totum hoc, non est intelligens et sapiens sicut tu.<div eID="gen5121" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen5122" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">40 </hi>Thou shalt be over my house, and according unto thy word shall all my people be ruled: only in the throne will I be greater than thou.<div eID="gen5122" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen5123" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">40. </hi>Tu eris super domum meam, et ad os tuum osculabitur omnis populus meus: tantum solio major ero to.<div eID="gen5123" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen5124" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">41. </hi>And Pharaoh said unto Joseph, See, I have set thee over all the land of Egypt.<div eID="gen5124" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen5125" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">41. </hi>Itaque dixit Pharao ad Joseph, Vide, posui to super totam terram Aegypti.<div eID="gen5125" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen5126" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">42. </hi>And Pharaoh took off his ring from his hand, and put it upon Joseph’s hand, and arrayed him in vestures of fine linen, and put a gold chain about his neck;<div eID="gen5126" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen5127" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">42. </hi>Et removit Pharao annulum suum e manu sua, posuitque illum in manu Joseph: et indui fecit eum vestibus byssinis, et posuit torquem aureum in collo ejus.<div eID="gen5127" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen5128" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">43. </hi>And he made him to ride in the second chariot which he had; and they cried before him, Bow the knee: and he made him <hi type="italic">ruler</hi> over all the land of Egypt.<div eID="gen5128" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen5129" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">43. </hi>Et equitare fecit eum in curru secundi, qui erat apud se, clamabantque ante eum, Albrech, (id est, pater tener,) et constituit cum super universam terram Aegypti<div eID="gen5129" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen5130" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">44. </hi>And Pharaoh said unto Joseph, I <hi type="italic">am</hi> Pharaoh, and without thee shall no man lift up his hand or foot in all the land of Egypt.<div eID="gen5130" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen5131" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">44. </hi>Dixit ergo Pharao ad Joseph, Ego Pharao, et sine, to non levabit quisquam manum suam et pedem suum in tota terra Aegypti.<div eID="gen5131" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen5132" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">45. </hi>And Pharaoh called Joseph’s name Zaphnathpaaneah; and he gave him to wife Asenath the daughter of Potipherah priest of On. And Joseph went out over <hi type="italic">all</hi> the land of Egypt.<div eID="gen5132" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen5133" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">45. </hi>Et vocavit Pharao nomen Joseph, Saphenath — Paneah, (id est, vir cui abscondita revelata sunt, vel, absconditorum expositor,) et dedit ei Asenath filiam Poti — pherah principis On in uxorem, et egressus est Joseph super terram Aegypti.<div eID="gen5133" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen5134" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">46. </hi>And Joseph <hi type="italic">was</hi> thirty years old when he stood before Pharaoh king of Egypt. And Joseph went out from the presence of Pharaoh, and went throughout all the land of Egypt.<div eID="gen5134" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen5135" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">46. </hi>Joseph vero erat vir triginta annorum, quando stetit coram Pharaone rege Aegypti: et egressus est Joseph a facie Pharaonis, et transivit per totam terram Aegypti.<div eID="gen5135" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen5136" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">47. </hi>And in the seven plenteous years the earth brought forth by handfuls.<div eID="gen5136" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen5137" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">47. </hi>Et protulit terra septem annis saturitatis ad collectiones.<div eID="gen5137" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen5138" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">48. </hi>And he gathered up all the food of the seven years, which were in the land of Egypt, and laid up the food in the cities: the food of the field, which <hi type="italic">was</hi> round about every city, laid he up in the same.<div eID="gen5138" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen5139" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">48. </hi>Et congregavit de universis cibis septem annorum, qui fuerunt in terra Aegypti, et posuit cibum in urbibus: cibum agri civitatis, qui erat in circuitu ejus, posuit in medio ejus.<div eID="gen5139" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen5140" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">49. </hi>And Joseph gathered corn as the sand of the sea, very much, until he left numbering; for <hi type="italic">it was</hi> without number.<div eID="gen5140" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen5141" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">49. </hi>Congregavit itaque Joseph frumentum, tanquam arenam maris multum valde, adeo ut cessaverit numerari, quia non erat numerus.<div eID="gen5141" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen5142" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">50. </hi>And unto Joseph were born two sons before the years of famine came, which Asenath the daughter of Potipherah priest of On bare unto him.<div eID="gen5142" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen5143" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">50. </hi>Porro ipsi Joseph nati sunt duo filii antequam veniret annus famis, quos peperit ei Asenath filia Poti — pherah principis On.<div eID="gen5143" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen5144" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">51.</hi> And Joseph called the name of the firstborn Manasseh: For God, <hi type="italic">said he</hi>, hath made me forget all my toil, and all my father’s house.<div eID="gen5144" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen5145" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">51. </hi>Et vocavit Joseph nomen primogeniti, Menasseh: quia dixit, Oblivisci fecit me Deus omnis laboris mei, et omnis domus patris mei.<div eID="gen5145" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen5146" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">52. </hi>And the name of the second called he Ephraim: For God hath caused me to be fruitful in the land of my affliction.<div eID="gen5146" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen5147" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">52. </hi>Nomen autem secundi vocavit Ephraim: quia dixit, crescere fecit me Deus in terra afflictionbis meae.<div eID="gen5147" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen5148" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">53. </hi>And the seven years of plenteousness, that was in the land of Egypt, were ended.<div eID="gen5148" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen5149" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">53. </hi>Et finit sunt septem anni saturitatis, quae fuit in terra Aegypti.<div eID="gen5149" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen5150" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">54. </hi>And the seven years of dearth began to come, according as Joseph had said: and the dearth was in all lands; but in all the land of Egypt there was bread.<div eID="gen5150" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen5151" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">54. </hi>Inceperunt vero septem anni famis venire, quemadmodum dixerat Joseph, fuitque fames in omnibus terris: at in tota terra Aegypti erat panis.<div eID="gen5151" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen5152" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">55. </hi>And when all the land of Egypt was famished, the people cried to Pharaoh for bread: and Pharaoh said unto all the Egyptians, Go unto Joseph; what he saith to you, do.<div eID="gen5152" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen5153" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">55. </hi>Postea esuriit tota terra Aegypti, et clamavit populus ad Pharaonem pro pane: et dixit Pharao omnibus Aegyptiis, Ite ad Joseph, quod dixerit vobis, facietis.<div eID="gen5153" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen5154" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">56.</hi> And the famine was over all the face of the earth: And Joseph opened all the storehouses, and sold unto the Egyptians; and the famine waxed sore in the land of Egypt.<div eID="gen5154" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen5155" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">56. </hi>Et fames erat in omni superficie terrae: et aperuit Joseph omnia horrea, in quibus erant frumenta, et vendidit Aegyptiis: et invaluit fames in terra Aegypti.<div eID="gen5155" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen5156" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">57.</hi> And all countries came into Egypt to Joseph for to buy <hi type="italic">corn</hi>; because that the famine was <hi type="italic">so</hi> sore in all lands.<div eID="gen5156" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen5157" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">57.</hi> Et omnes habitatores terrae venerunt in Aegyptum, ut emerent a Joseph: quia invaluerat fames in omni terra.<div eID="gen5157" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row> </table>                   <ns0:p n="14">14 But <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> remem<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ber me with thee.</ns0:note> think on me, when it shall be well with thee, and shew kindness, I pray thee, unto me, and make mention of me unto Pharaoh, and bring me out of this house <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">Though he patiently endures his prison, yet he prudent<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly useth all lawful means to get his freedom.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="15">15 For indeed I was stollen away <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">Taken away by force and fraud without my own or Fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thers consent.</ns0:note> out of the land of the Hebrews <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">Out of the land of <ns0:hi>Canaan,</ns0:hi> which he might call <ns0:hi>the Land of Hebrews,</ns0:hi> either because they now <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">

Or rather thus, out of that part of <ns0:hi>Canaan</ns0:hi> where the He<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />brews dwell: For the word <ns0:hi>Land</ns0:hi> is not onely spoken of whole Countries, as of the whole Land of <ns0:hi>Canaan,</ns0:hi> but of any parts or parcels thereof, as <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 13. 6. and 22. 2. and 23. 15. and 34. 1.</ns0:note>, and here also have I done nothing <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">Observe, that <ns0:hi>Ioseph</ns0:hi> doth not accuse either his bre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thren or his mistress, but onely asserts his own innocency, which was necessary for his deliverance.</ns0:note>, that they should put me into the dun<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />geon.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="16">

                        </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> white <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">So called from the colour either of the baskets, which were made of pilled and so white twigs, or of the things contain<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed in them as white bread, &c.</ns0:note> baskets on my head.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="17">17 And in the uppermost basket there was of all manner of <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">

                  <ns0:p n="18">18 And Joseph answered, and said, This is the interpretation thereof: the three baskets <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> three days:</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="19">19 Yet within three days shall Pharaoh <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>reckon thee,</ns0:hi> and take thy office from thee.</ns0:note> lift up thy head from <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">This clause is industriously added here to the former phrase, to shew that it was now meant in another sense, He <ns0:hi>shall</ns0:hi> in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />deed <ns0:hi>lift up thy head,</ns0:hi> as well as the chief Bakers, but in ano<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther manner, not for thee, but <ns0:hi>from thee,</ns0:hi> or so as to take away thy head or thy Life (which eminently consists and appears in the head) from thee.</ns0:note> off thee: and shall hang thee on a tree, and the birds shall eat thy flesh from off thee.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="20">20 And it came to pass the third day <ns0:hi>which was</ns0:hi> Pharaohs birth-day <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">Which by persons of eminency then was and since hath usually been celebrated with feasting and rejoycing.</ns0:note>, that he <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Mark 6. 21</ns0:note> made a feast un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />to all his servants: and he <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Or,</ns0:hi> reckoned.</ns0:note> lifted up the head of the chief Butler, and of the chief Baker among his servants.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="21">21 And he restored the chief Butler unto his butlership again, and he gave the cup into Phara<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ohs hand.</ns0:p>
